clue.text: Crack reversed in cracker (French, as with nuts)

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed within the other piece

parts.note: casse, from the French casse-noix, nutcracker; casser means to crack
REV is the standard abbreviation for reverse or reversed

explanation.surface: A recipe-like note on cracking nuts the French way, with a crack turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' looks like a reversal signal but simply supplies its abbreviation REV.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep split in a glacier, a crack in the ice.

clue.text: Woody shrub contains wild beast within some limits

indicators.note: within says the beast's letters are placed inside the shortened word
some means only part of the word limits is used, its last letters dropped

parts.note: the gnu, or wildebeest, a wild beast of Africa

explanation.surface: A botanical note on a shrub that keeps an animal penned inside its bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' trims limits to LIM (ITS dropped); 'contains' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lignum is a tangled Australian plant of floodplains, a wiry shrub; the Latin word means wood.

clue.text: Spooner's suspended herb at scene of cockcrow

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words, after Rev Spooner

parts.note: suspended means hung up
dill is a feathery culinary herb

explanation.surface: Dried herbs hanging up somewhere a cockerel crows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel traditionally stands crowing on the farmyard manure heap.

clue.text: Cook last of cheese in front of radiator

parts.note: to grill is to cook under direct heat

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word cheese

explanation.surface: Instructions to toast cheese before setting it by the heater.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is the grating across the front of a car's radiator.

clue.text: Insect's 22 with cover for a larger one

parts.note: 22 is the clue for a part of the body; an ear is one
a wig covers the head, a body part larger than an ear

explanation.surface: Something about an insect's organ, with a covering for a bigger one.
explanation.definitionFit: The earwig is a common insect with pincers at its tail.

clue.text: Rivers rose so as to form subject of comedy

indicators.note: so as to form says the letters are rearranged into something new

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for river, so two rivers give two Rs

explanation.surface: Rivers rising high enough to make a funny story.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's The Comedy of Errors takes its name from mistakes, the subject of the play.

clue.text: Rotten rubbish raised retrospectively

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking backwards, so the whole run is read in reverse

parts.note: dirt is filth or rubbish
raised means up

explanation.surface: Junk dug up again when looking back on things.
explanation.walkthrough: DIRTUP read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Putrid food has gone off, decayed and foul-smelling, so rotten.

clue.text: Talk endlessly about cast object

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to discuss is to talk about something

explanation.surface: Going on and on about a thing that has been thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' just links, part of the phrase 'talk about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus is the heavy disc thrown by athletes, an object for casting.

clue.text: Mosley's lot boycotts Hirst's work

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, in trade-union usage

indicators.note: work signals the name is worked into a new order

parts.note: Damien Hirst the artist; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A fascist group refusing to look at a Damien Hirst piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Oswald Mosley led the British Union of Fascists, whose members wore black uniforms.

clue.text: Yellow 22s in Shropshire

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, a synonym
upper limbs, each one a part of the body

explanation.surface: Cowardly limbs found in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: SHROPSHIRE is a rural English county on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small market town lying in that West Midlands county, named after an inn.

clue.text: Stickler with 22 on a table

parts.note: a leg is a part of the body
a list or table of items

explanation.surface: A fussy person with a limb resting on a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A legalist insists rigidly on the letter of the law, a stickler for rules.

clue.text: See 9
Mother's 22, say, a French weapon

parts.note: ma is mother, the possessive adding no letter
the chin is a part of the body
say signals an example, eg
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Mum's jaw described as a French weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an automatic firearm firing bullets in rapid succession.

clue.text: Problem with a 22, a number of new lines to the front

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: new signals the word lines is made new by rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A ailment tied to some fresh lines of verse being put at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal on 'lines', and 'the front' is a ship's front, not the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an inflamed tendon at the outer joint of the arm, from repetitive strain.

clue.text: Bean meal could be worth mentioning

indicators.note: could be says these letters may become another word

explanation.surface: Ground beans might just merit a mention.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be named is fit to be mentioned, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Gall authorised around a part of 25

indicators.note: around says the first piece goes round the letter that follows

parts.note: OK means authorised or approved
25 begins with the eye, and the pupil is the apple of the eye

explanation.surface: Approved gall around part of something else in the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak apple is a round swelling on oak trees caused by a wasp, a type of gall.

clue.text: Pass the Guardian's standard

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
the newspaper speaking of itself says our

explanation.surface: Hand over the newspaper's banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's colour is its flag or standard.

clue.text: Protection for 22 that gives direction to film

parts.note: the helm steers a ship, giving it direction
ET is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Safety gear for a part of the body and guidance for a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet is head protection worn against blows.

clue.text: Problem for a 22: some haikus need translating

indicators.note: translating turns these words into different letters

explanation.surface: Some Japanese poems need putting into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: It is bursitis of the joint in the leg, from long kneeling at scrubbing floors.

clue.text: A year in prison's half wanting observation

indicators.note: in signals A and the year going inside
half wanting says half of the prison's name is missing, leaving one half

parts.note: Sing Sing is the New York state prison
Y is year

explanation.surface: A year inside, with half of something missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The prison is Sing Sing, so half of it is a single word that then holds A and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A saying is a remark or proverb, an observation.

clue.text: Transformer of Cambridge college with one change of direction

indicators.note: change of direction swaps one compass point for another

parts.note: Selwyn is a Cambridge college

explanation.surface: Something altering a university college, with a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A selsyn is a self-synchronous electrical device, a kind of rotary transformer.

clue.text: See 18
Maybe head of telecommunicators accepting inverted burlesque

indicators.note: accepting says the company takes the other piece inside

parts.note: BT, British Telecom, the phone company

indicators.note: inverted means the two halves of the word are turned about

parts.note: a burlesque is a parody

explanation.surface: Perhaps a phone company boss putting up with satire turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' here swaps the two halves of the burlesque word rather than reading it backwards; 'accepting' puts that inside the phone company.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is one example of a portion of the anatomy.

clue.text: Tumour in 22, with love — mother

parts.note: the lip is a part of the body
love is nil, O in tennis
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A growth on the mouth, with love from Mum.
explanation.definitionFit: A lipoma is a benign fatty tumour under the skin.

clue.text: Right 22 will not be forgotten

parts.note: the ankle is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A properly hurt joint will stay in the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance that rankles keeps festering in the mind, unforgotten.

clue.text: 22 with permitted hole

parts.note: the eye is a part of the body
let means permitted

explanation.surface: A part of the body allowed through a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small reinforced hole for a lace or cord.
